name: p5-toledo-war
style: General American accent. Calm, confident documentary narrator with dry wit, like explaining a map to a curious friend. Conversational, not hyped. Slightly slower on numbers, dates and place names. Maumee is pronounced "MAW-mee". "Blame Toledo." is dry and deadpan. "So who got hurt?" is a light question; "One sheriff." is short, after a tiny pause. Before "Two Stickney" take a small comic pause. "Iron. And copper." lands slowly, one beat apart. The last two sentences are calm and a little slower, falling at the end. Never shout.

lines.text: In 1787, Congress drew a line straight east from the bottom of Lake Michigan.
One problem: the maps of the day put the lake too far north.
Ohio's survey put the line above the mouth of the Maumee River, and the town of Toledo.
Michigan's survey followed the 1787 law, and kept Toledo.
Between them: a strip up to eight miles wide.
By 1835, both sides were ready for war.

lines.text: Then Congress made an offer: give Ohio the strip, take the western Upper Peninsula instead.
Then, in a freezing December, it said yes.
Some say the Ohio State–Michigan rivalry started right here.
In 1844, a surveyor named William Burt watched his compass needle go haywire.
The ground under him was full of iron.
Then, for forty years, Michigan mined more copper than any other state.
